chunks: From him, from al-‘Abbās, from Ṣafwān, from a man, from Abī Baṣīr and others, from Abī ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said: If the one being stoned flees from the pit, is he to be pursued? He said: “No, and he is not to be confronted, if a single stone has struck him, he is not pursued. But if he flees before the stones strike him, he is returned until the pain of the punishment reaches him.”

key_terms.الْحَفِيرَةِ: the pit from which the condemned person is stoned
key_terms.الْحِجَارَةُ: the stones used in carrying out the punishment
key_terms.الْمَرْجُومُ: the person upon whom stoning is being carried out
key_terms.حَجَرٌ وَاحِدٌ: a single stone, indicating the punishment has already begun
key_terms.يُطْلَبُ: he is pursued and sought after

ai.seo_question: If a person sentenced to stoning escapes after the punishment has begun, should he be pursued and returned?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a person undergoing rajm who flees from the pit during the punishment. It states that if even one stone has already struck him, he is not to be pursued, but if he flees before any stone reaches him, he is returned so that the punishment begins upon him.
